header.title: Cyranides: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Cyranides
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg1482.tlg001.1st1K-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg1482.tlg001.1st1K-gr: '[ἄλλων]', 'other', is bracketed in the edition, apparently as superfluous. 'Those in power' renders περιεχόντων, whose sense here (the powerful, or the wealthy) is uncertain.

nodes.text: So take an eagle-stone and engrave an eagle [on it], and under the stone put a grape-seed and the tip of a feather of the eagle, or of a hawk, and enclose [it] and wear it; for it will guard you from all the afflictions mentioned above. Moreover it will make [you] esteemed and well liked in meetings with rulers, and will win you the favour of great men and of those in power; and it will work in many other [further] matters which there is no need to tell. And so the first letter, Alpha, has come to its end.
